en: Udāna 4.8 Sundarīsutta Thus have I heard—
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
At that time, the Blessed One was honored, revered, esteemed, venerated, and respected, and he received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.
The Saṅgha of bhikkhus was also honored, revered, esteemed, venerated, and respected, and it received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.

But the wanderers of other sects were unhonored, unrespected, undervalued, unworshipped, and uncared for, and they did not receive gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.

Then those wanderers of other sects, unable to endure the veneration accorded to the Blessed One and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, approached the female wanderer Sundarī; having approached her, they said this to the female wanderer Sundarī:
“Sister, are you able to act for the benefit of your kinsmen?”
“What can I do, noble lady?
What is there that I cannot do?
Even my own life has been surrendered for the sake of my kinsmen.”
“In that case, sister, go frequently to Jeta’s Grove.
“Very well, lady,” Sundarī the wanderer replied to those wanderers of other sects, and she went frequently to Jeta’s Grove.
When those wanderers of other sects came to know this:
“Sundarī the female wanderer has indeed been seen frequently going to Jeta’s Grove by many people.

Then, having deprived her of life and buried her right there in a pit in the moat of Jeta’s Grove, they approached King Pasenadi of Kosala. Having approached, they said this to King Pasenadi of Kosala:
“That female wanderer Sundarī, Your Majesty, is not to be seen by us.”
“But where did you suspect [him], sirs?
“In Jeta’s Grove, Great King.
“In that case, search Jeta’s Grove.”
Then those wanderers of other sects, having searched through Jetavana, pulled up the moat-pits as they had been placed,
put them onto a litter, and brought them into Sāvatthī; going from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads,
they incited the people to indignation:
“Look, venerable ones, at the work of these recluses, the sons of the Sakyan!
These recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, are shameless, immoral, of evil character, speakers of falsehood, and unchaste.
Yet they claim to be practitioners of the Dhamma, practitioners of integrity, practitioners of the holy life, speakers of truth, virtuous, and of beautiful character!”
There is no asceticism in them; there is no brahminhood in them.
Asceticism has been lost by them; brahminhood has been lost by them.
Wherein lies their asceticism? Wherein lies their brahminhood?
“These have departed from the state of a recluse; these have departed from the state of a brahmin.
How indeed could a man, having performed his duty as a man, deprive a woman of life?
Now at that time, people in Sāvatthī, upon seeing monks, reviled, abused, incensed, and harassed them with improper and harsh words:
“Shameless are these recluses, sons of the Sakyans; they are immoral, of evil character, speakers of falsehood, and unchaste.
Yet they claim to be practitioners of the Dhamma, practitioners of integrity, practitioners of the holy life, speakers of truth, virtuous, and of beautiful character.
There is no true asceticism in them, there is no true brahminhood in them.”
The state of a recluse has been lost by these, the state of a brahmin has been lost by these.
From where could they have the state of a recluse? From where could they have the state of a brahmin?
These have departed from the state of a recluse; these have departed from the state of a brahmin.
“How indeed could a man, having performed his duty as a man, deprive a woman of life?
Then, in the morning, a number of bhikkhus dressed themselves, took their bowls and robes, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.
Having walked for alms in Sāvatthī, after their meal, returning from their almsround, they approached the Blessed One.
Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
Sitting there, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:
"At present, Bhante, when people in Sāvatthī see the bhikkhus, they revile, abuse, irritate, and harass them with improper and harsh words, saying: [text continues]"
‘These ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, are shameless, immoral, of evil nature, liars, and unchaste.
Yet they claim to be practitioners of the Dhamma, practitioners of equanimity, practitioners of the holy life, speakers of truth, virtuous, and of noble character.
They possess neither the state of a recluse nor the state of a brahmin.’
The state of a recluse is lost for these; the state of a brahmin is lost for these.
Where is the state of a recluse for these? Where is the state of a brahmin for these?
These have departed from the state of a recluse; these have departed from the state of a brahmin.
“How indeed could a man, having performed his duty as a man, deprive a woman of life?
“Monks, this sound will not last long; it will last for only seven days. After the passing of seven days, it will disappear.
Therefore, monks, when people see you bhikkhus and revile, abuse, irritate, or harass you with unseemly and harsh words, you should rebuke them with this verse:”
“The speaker of what is untrue goes to hell,
as does he who, having done something, says, ‘I did not do it.
Both of them, having passed away, become equal.”
"Men of base deeds for the sake of others.

Then those bhikkhus, having mastered this verse in the presence of the Blessed One, [recited it] toward those people who, upon seeing the bhikkhus, reviled, abused, enraged, and harassed them with improper and harsh words. With this—
They rebuked him with this verse:
"The speaker of untruth goes to hell, as does he who,
having done something, says, 'I did not do it.'"
"Both of them, having passed away, become equal in the next world,
those men who have performed base deeds.
Then this thought occurred to the people:
“These ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, are non-doers; nothing is done by them; these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, are powerless.
That sound did not last long. It lasted only seven days. With the passing of seven days, it vanished. Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One;
having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:
“It is wonderful, Bhante! It is marvelous, Bhante!
How well this has been spoken by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, this sound will not last long; it will last for only seven days. With the passing of seven days, it will disappear.’”
“Venerable sir, that sound has vanished.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Unrestrained people pierce others with their speech;”
Just as an elephant in battle facing the enemy,
so too, having heard harsh words spoken,
a bhikkhu should endure them with a mind free from malice.
The eighth.
